title: The 10 Best Electric Demolition Hammers
subtitle: Electric demolition and jack hammers for tile removal, chipping and breaking concrete, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: An electric demolition hammer chisels without drilling: light ones strip tile and mortar, heavy ones break slabs. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Berserker, VEVOR, XtremepowerUS, ENEACRO and Makita on rating, review volume and features (a listed impact energy, vibration control, chisels and a case in the box). Wattage claims on this category run high, so compare amps and joules instead.

products.name: XtremepowerUS 2200W Demolition Jack Hammer with Flat and Bull Point Chisels, Concrete Breaker
products.verdict: The best-selling and most-reviewed jack hammer here, sold with 16-inch point and flat chisels, gloves, goggles and a carrying case. It lists a 20-amp draw, more than a standard 15-amp household circuit is meant to supply.
products.best_for: Breaking up a patio, sidewalk or footing on a budget.
products.skip_if: You'll run it from a standard 15 A garage outlet all day; it lists 20 A.
pros: Chisels, gloves, goggles and case included

products.name: Berserker 1300W 12-Pound SDS-Max Demolition Jack Hammer 45HM, 11-Amp
products.verdict: A light 12 lb SDS-Max chipping hammer for tile, thinset and light concrete, with 12 chisel positions. It's hammer-only, with no drilling mode.
products.best_for: Tile and mortar removal, and chipping overhead or on walls.
products.skip_if: You need to break thick slabs; 15 J is light-duty.

products.name: VEVOR Demolition Jack Hammer, MAX 1400W, 2900 BPM, 2 Chisels, Case, Gloves
products.verdict: The cheapest jack hammer here, with two chisels, gloves, a case and a shock-absorbing handle. It's rated 19 J, enough for tile and light chipping.
products.best_for: Occasional tile, mortar and thin concrete jobs.
products.skip_if: You're breaking 4-inch slabs; step up to a 45 J+ breaker.

products.name: Berserker 1700W 30-Pound Demolition Jack Hammer 65F with 1-3/16" Hex, 14 Amp
products.verdict: A heavy 31 lb breaker that turns its weight into 55 J of impact energy for slabs and footings, with anti-vibration tech and a longer air cushion. It takes 1-3/16 inch hex bits only.
products.best_for: Breaking concrete slabs, driveways and footings.
products.skip_if: You need to work on walls or overhead; it's 31 lb.

products.name: VEVOR Demolition Jack Hammer, MAX 2200W, 1350 BPM, 6 Chisels, with Case
products.verdict: A large VEVOR breaker sold with six chisels (point, flat, two spades and two scrapers), a 360-degree side handle and a carrying case.
products.best_for: Breaking slabs and digging hard ground with one kit.
products.skip_if: You want specs you can trust; the listing's 6.3 A and 15,500 rpm fields don't fit a 2,200 W breaker.
cons: Listing's amp and rpm fields contradict the wattage

products.name: ENEACRO ENDH45 SDS-Max Demolition Jack Hammer, 11 Amp
products.verdict: A light SDS-Max chipping hammer like the Berserker 45HM, with an anti-scald front housing and 4.7 stars, the highest-rated breaker here.

products.name: Berserker 1300W 12-Pound SDS-Max Demolition Jack Hammer 45HMC, 11-Amp Corded
products.verdict: A 12 lb SDS-Max chipping hammer with 15 J, 12-position chisel lock and anti-vibration handling. Comes with three chisels, a spare brush and a case. Hammer only, no drilling.
products.best_for: Tile, thinset and mortar removal where a light tool matters.
products.skip_if: You're breaking thick slabs; 15 J is light for that.
pros: Three SDS-Max chisels and a case

products.name: Makita HM0870C 11-Pound Demolition Hammer, SDS-Max
products.verdict: The only big-brand demolition hammer here: Makita's 11 lb SDS-Max hammer with constant speed control that holds speed under load, soft start, and a tool case.
products.best_for: Pros who chip and demo every week and want a tool built to last.
products.skip_if: You need a slab breaker; this is a chipping hammer.
pros: Constant speed control and soft start
cons: Lower impact energy than the cheap breakers claim

products.name: XtremepowerUS 1400W Electric Demolition Jack Hammer, 3900 BPM, 5/8" Hex, Point & Flat Chisels
products.verdict: A lighter XtremepowerUS hammer with 3,900 BPM, vibration-reducing handles, a trigger lock, point and flat chisels and a carrying case.
products.best_for: Tile and light chipping on a budget.

products.name: BOSCH 11316EVS 14 Amp SDS-Max Demolition Hammer with Variable Speed
products.verdict: A contractor-grade 23 lb SDS-Max hammer with soft start, constant speed under load, a variable speed dial, a padded shock-absorbing rear handle and a service light.
products.best_for: Contractors who run a demo hammer for hours at a time.
products.skip_if: You have a weekend tile job; the cheaper breakers here will do it.

avoid.name: VEVOR Demolition Jack Hammer, 3500W Jack Hammer Concrete Breaker 1900 BPM, 2 Chisels, Gloves
avoid.flag: Claims 3,500 W; its own spec table says 13 A
avoid.verdict: The listing advertises a 3,500 W motor and 60 J, but its own spec table lists 13 amps at 110 V, about 1,430 W.
reasons: 'MAX 3500W' is more than any household outlet can supply: a 15 A, 120 V circuit tops out around 1,800 W.
The same listing's spec table says 13 A at 110 V, which works out to roughly 1,430 W, less than half the headline number.
With the power figure inflated, the 60 J impact claim can't be taken at face value either. Berserker's 65F lists 55 J from a 14 A motor and is rated 4.6 stars.

buyers_guide.q: Demolition hammer, jack hammer or rotary hammer?
buyers_guide.a: A rotary hammer drills and chisels. A demolition (chipping) hammer only chisels; most here say 'hammer only, no drilling.' 'Jack hammer' on Amazon usually means a bigger electric breaker for slabs. Real pavement breakers weigh 60+ lb.

buyers_guide.q: How much impact energy do I need?
buyers_guide.a: About 10 to 20 J removes tile, thinset and mortar. 40 to 65 J breaks 4-inch concrete slabs and footings. More energy means more weight, so match the tool to the job.

Not always. A standard 15 A, 120 V outlet supplies about 1,800 W, so listings claiming 2,200 or 3,500 W are quoting a peak, not continuous power. Amps and impact energy (joules or ft-lb) are more useful.
SDS-Max is the standard for demolition hammers up to about 25 lb and bits are easy to find. Bigger breakers use 1-1/8 or 1-3/16 inch hex. Buy bits that match your tool exactly.

buyers_guide.q: What safety gear do I need?
buyers_guide.a: Eye protection, hearing protection, gloves and a dust mask or respirator: breaking concrete makes silica dust. Wet the surface or use a vacuum shroud where you can.
